html:
The Slave Abolition Act of 1905, under which King Chulalongkorn completed the end of slavery in Siam after three decades of gradual steps.

Slavery in Siam went back to the Ayutthaya period. Most slaves were debt slaves, who had sold themselves or their children to pay what they owed, and a large share of the people of central Siam were in some form of bondage in the mid 1800s. Others were war captives.

Chulalongkorn moved carefully, because nobles depended on slave labour. In 1874 he decreed that children born to slaves since his accession in 1868 would be free at 21, and capped the price at which people could be sold. Later laws freed more groups, and the 1905 act ended the practice.

The reform went with others: a salaried civil service, conscription in place of old labour duties, and new taxes. It fit his wider plan to make Siam look modern in European eyes and so harder to colonise. Unlike the American Civil War, it cost no war, and unlike the British Slavery Abolition Act it paid no compensation.
sum: The Slave Abolition Act of 1905, under which King Chulalongkorn completed the end of slavery in Siam after three decades of gradual steps.
